observed: validate_checkpoint() skips all claim/checkpoint identity checks when claim is None.
The validator does not consume or validate workpackages/active/<workpackage_id>.json.
The regression suite tests claim mismatch only when a claim object is supplied and does not pin rejection of claim-less validation.
finding.consequence: A syntactically valid checkpoint can receive validator PASS without proving that its workpackage/generation/claim identity is the repository's current mutation-authority chain. This is weaker than the fail-closed identity consistency required by WORKER_PROTOCOL.md and CLAIM_PROTOCOL.md.
finding.counterhypothesis: The validator may intentionally support a syntax-only mode and a higher-level caller may separately require --claim and active-pointer validation. No such higher-level binding was observed in the reviewed source/tests, so acceptance must not rely on that assumption without explicit evidence.
finding.cheapest_discriminator: Add a regression invoking validation without a claim and require fail-closed rejection for canonical CURRENT validation, or introduce an explicit non-authoritative syntax-only mode distinct from canonical validation; canonical validation should additionally bind the active pointer identity/state to the checkpoint and claim.
